name: Sustainable Communities Challenge Fund
summary: Provincial climate-action grants for Nova Scotia community organizations; the adaptation stream funds ecosystem and nature-based projects such as coastal restoration, alongside mitigation work like buildings and energy.
reporting: Brief quarterly progress reports; after completion a final impact report with a financial report.

eligibility.rule: If a non-profit: NS society or co-op, Canadian charity or federal non-profit operating in NS
Project is based in Nova Scotia and meets at least one core objective
Organisation submits no more than two applications in an intake round
Previous grantee is in good standing with its prior project before reapplying
Round 4 project is fully completed by November 30, 2027
Project is a community priority, shown by consultation, a community plan or a council letter

applicant_types.quote: The following groups are eligible lead applicants: Nova Scotia municipalities First Nations bands and tribal councils Post-secondary institutions Non-profit organizations operating in Nova Scotia

geography.quote: The Sustainable Communities Challenge Fund is a provincial grant program for local action on climate change in Nova Scotia.

access.quote: Create an account and log into the Submittable portal to complete the pre-screening form.

amount.quote: The Fund will provide non-repayable grants between $75,000 and $1,000,000 per project that range from 60 - 80% of eligible project costs.

co_finance_required.quote: An applicant must make a financial contribution to the project, and their overall contribution may be a combination of cash and in-kind according to the cost-sharing requirements below.

reporting.quote: Recipients are required to provide brief quarterly progress reports on whether their project is on track and any challenges they are experiencing. Upon project completion recipients submit a Final Impact Report, including a financial report on how the Fund was spent,

eligibility.quote: Registered, Nova Scotia-based, non-profit societies/ cooperatives in good standing; Registered Canadian charities actively operating in Nova Scotia; or Federally incorporated non-profit organizations operating in Nova Scotia.
To be eligible, projects must be based in Nova Scotia and must meet at least one of the two core objectives (mitigation or adaptation).
Organizations may submit a maximum of two applications for consideration in each intake round.
Organizations that have received a grant from the Fund can reapply if they are in good standing with their prior project.
All Round 4 projects must be fully completed by November 30, 2027.

a community priority. This could be demonstrated by providing evidence of consultation or engagement and buy-in, it could be identified in a community plan/municipal document or by having a letter of support from a municipal council.

co_finance.quote: A minimum of 20% of eligible project costs must be contributed by the applicant. The financial contribution may be made by project partners or alternate funding sources such as federal funding. In-kind contributions such as staff time can count toward the applicant's contribution to a maximum of 10%.

after_award.quote: Recipients are required to provide brief quarterly progress reports on whether their project is on track and any challenges they are experiencing.
